prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” broker for every self‑employed person in Kansas City — the right choice depends on your budget, health needs, whether you want in‑person help, and whether you qualify for marketplace subsidies. Instead of naming one firm as best, here’s a straightforward way to find the best broker for you plus free help options.

What to look for in a broker
- Licensed in Missouri and in good standing with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance.
- Experience with individual & family (ACA) plans and with self‑employed clients (1099/sole proprietors).
- Independent agent (can offer multiple carrier options) rather than captive to one insurer.
- Transparent about fees vs. commission and whether they’ll charge you directly.
- Will compare multiple carriers, explain networks, deductibles, total out‑of‑pocket costs, and whether your doctors are in‑network.
- Good reviews or references and clear communication.

Places to get help (free or low cost)
- Healthcare.gov (federal Marketplace) — you can shop plans yourself and get premium tax credits if eligible.
- Certified Navigators/Assisters — offer free, unbiased enrollment help for Marketplace plans. I can look up navigator organizations near you if you give a ZIP code.
- Local independent agents — they can show multiple carriers and often help year‑round (not just at open enrollment).

How to evaluate specific brokers (questions to ask)
- “How many carriers and individual plans do you typically present?”
- “Do you charge a broker fee or work only by commission?”
- “Do you help with enrollment and renewals year‑round?”
- “Have you worked with other self‑employed clients like me? Any references?”
- “Which carriers do you recommend for my ZIP, budget, and preferred doctors?”

Where to start right now
- If you want free help: tell me your ZIP code and I’ll find local certified navigators and a few well‑reviewed independent agents in Kansas City who specialize in individual/self‑employed clients.
- If you want to shop yourself: go to Healthcare.gov, enter your ZIP, and compare plans and subsidy eligibility; then use a local independent agent to review your top options.

If you share your ZIP code, monthly budget or income range (for subsidy estimates), and whether you need specific doctors or prescriptions covered, I’ll pull up 3–5 local broker/agent options and navigator resources and give a short vetting summary for each. Which would you prefer?
